description: We want to make a roblox game to spark interest of space exploration to the youth and nuture their understanding and inspire them to pursue a career in the field
summary:
Outpost 07 is a free Roblox game that turns real Moon-mission constraints into a game meant for kids aged 7–12. They role-play as the crew of a small outpost at the lunar south pole, where NASA's Artemis program plans to land, and they're tasked to keep it alive for seven nights until a rescue ship arrives. Currently the game is rated as 16+ as we lack the funds to request verification from Roblox.
Every action has real impact. Melting ice into drinking water uses power. The
greenhouse grows food but drinks water and power. Fixing the radiation shelter
uses scrap. The emergency reserves boosts one system but drains another: a power
boost runs fuel cells that burn stored oxygen. Calling Earth from the satellite dish
takes a real 2.6-second round trip, so help never arrives instantly.
The two storm nights are driven by real solar flares from NASA's DONKI space-weather database, fetched live each game. An X-class flare means a severe storm
with less warning; a quiet Sun means a mild one. Players see the real flare class and
date in the game. Each evening ends with a short quiz built from facts their guide,
Captain Nova, told them that day.
The problem: kids rarely get to feel why astronauts plan so carefully. The impact:
Roblox is already a platform where millions of children play, on phones, tablets and computers. Outpost 07 meets them there, so a ten-year-old leaves knowing why water, power and shielding compete on the Moon, and that the space weather they survived was real.
details:
The whole outpost: habitat dome, support module and airlock, greenhouse, radiation shelter, solar arrays, moon buggy and the lander home. (File: 1_outpost.jpg)

Approach. We chose Roblox because children aged 7–12 already play there, for free, on phones, tablets, computers and consoles. The mission runs on a day/night clock. Each day gives the crew a job that teaches one constraint (clean the solar panels, start the greenhouse, seal an oxygen leak, tune the storm shield, stock up on water). Each night tests whether they prepared. A short cinematic shows the journey: launch on Earth, lunar orbit, landing at the outpost, and Orion's return and splashdown at the end.

Survive: gather crater ice and collect scrap out on the surface, while suit air drains. (File: 2_survive_ice_and_scrap.jpg)Run the base: melt ice into water at the ice plant, and grow food in the greenhouse with Captain Nova. (File: 3_run_the_base_water_and_food.jpg)

Every choice costs something. Melting ice uses power. The greenhouse makes food but drinks water and power. The storm shield cuts radiation damage but drains power. Rebuilding the shelter uses scrap. The emergency reserve boosts one system by draining another. Players learn that power, water, air and shielding compete, just as they do for real mission planners.

Every choice costs something: Mission Control shows each switch's cost, and skipped jobs come back as night alarms. (File: 4_every_choice_costs.jpg)

NASA data. Each game fetches the last 30 days of solar flares from NASA's DONKI spaceweather database. The flare class sets how hard the storms on nights 5 and 7 hit: an Xclass flare means a severe storm with only 8 seconds of warning, a C-class flare a mild one. Players see the real flare class and date in the game. NASA LCROSS results (water ice in dark south-pole craters), LRO CRaTER radiation measurements, NASA Moon facts and the Orion return profile shape the rest of the rules.

Sources:

DONKI, LCROSS, NASA Moon Data

Real NASA data: sources are named in the game, and a live DONKI M1.1 flare from 8 Nov 2026 turns night 5 into a moderate storm with 12 seconds of warning. (File: 5_real_nasa_data.jpg)

Learning loop. Captain Nova, an astronaut guide, explains what is happening in plain words and answers "Ask about the Moon" with NASA facts. Every third answer is today's real DONKI flare. At sunset a three-question quiz uses the facts that player heard. It is graded on the server and rewards a perfect score with scrap.

Learn: Captain Nova shares today's real DONKI flare count, and the end-of-day quiz checks what each player heard. (File: 6_learn_nova_and_quiz.jpg)

Fair multiplayer. Up to a full crew can play together. Restarts are a crew vote. Radiation knocks out one player rather than ending the game for everyone, and the mission fails only if nobody is left standing.


Explore: drive the moon buggy across the craters, and watch the Curiosity rover drill rock samples. (File: 7_explore_buggy_and_rover.jpg)

Tools and technologies:

- Roblox Studio and Luau for the game, the server mission logic and the cutscenes.

- Roblox HttpService for the live NASA DONKI requests, with a checked archive as fallback.

- Blender and Claude for the lunar lander, rover and buggy models.

- Python for build tools and the trailer soundtrack.
